title: Diffusion MRI of gray matter microstructural profiles in healthy aging
title_zh: 健康老龄化中灰质微观结构剖面扩散MRI研究
abstract: Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) is a non-invasive magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) acquisition technique that can provide detailed information about brain microstructure. This methodology has historically been applied only to white matter tissue in the research context, but more recent literature suggests that diffusion MRI can also be applied to study microstructural alterations of gray matter tissue, including in healthy aging. The current narrative review evaluates diffusion MRI studies investigating age-related differences in gray matter microstructure and their implications for understanding cognitive function in healthy older adults. The studies reviewed here report widespread age-related differences in cortical (especially frontoparietal), hippocampal, and subcortical microstructure that is behaviorally relevant- especially for cognitive domains of learning and memory. Gray matter microstructure is consistently influenced by the presence of dementia-related pathology, physical activity, and sleep health, but additional research work is needed to understand the roles of biological sex, environment, and dietary intake. Future work of gray matter microstructural profiles in healthy aging should consider longitudinal designs, combining different diffusion MRI modeling techniques in the same study, and defining more specific cognitive correlates (e.g., processing speed).
abstract_zh: 扩散加权成像（DWI）是一种非侵入性磁共振成像（MRI）采集技术，可提供关于脑微结构的详细信息。该方法历来主要用于白质研究，但近期文献提示扩散MRI也可用于研究灰质微结构变化，包括健康老龄化中的变化。本文是一篇叙述性综述，评估了研究灰质微结构年龄相关差异的扩散MRI文献及其对健康老年人认知功能理解的意义。所综述研究报道了广泛的皮质（尤其是额顶叶）、海马和皮下核微结构随年龄变化，这些变化与行为相关，尤其与学习和记忆等认知领域相关。灰质微结构持续受到痴呆相关病理、身体活动和睡眠健康的影响，但尚需更多研究来阐明生物性别、环境和膳食摄入的作用。未来在健康老龄化背景下的灰质微结构剖面研究应考虑纵向设计，在同一研究中结合不同的扩散MRI建模技术，并定义更具体的认知相关指标（例如处理速度）。
